# Discovery call — Summit Ridge Roofing (held-out)

AJ: Thanks for jumping on, Carlos. Walk me through a normal week. Where does the time go that you wish it didn't?

Carlos: So we're a residential roofing company, about 120 roofs a year, almost all of it insurance work after hail and wind storms. The roofs are not the problem. The paperwork is the problem.

AJ: Say more.

Carlos: Every insurance claim needs a packet. Photos from CompanyCam, the EagleView measurements, our Xactimate estimate, the signed contingency agreement, and the adjuster's scope. My office manager, Tamara, puts every packet together by hand and uploads it to the carrier portal. That's probably 12 hours a week for her, and when she's out it just doesn't happen.

Carlos: And then the supplements. The adjuster misses stuff all the time, drip edge, starter, ice and water, code upgrades. We have to write a supplement with photos for every line they left off. We figure there's about $40,000 a month we just never collect because nobody had time to supplement it.

AJ: How long do claims sit?

Carlos: Too long. We have maybe 35 open claims right now. Some are waiting on the adjuster, some are waiting on the mortgage company to endorse the check. Nobody really tracks it, Tamara keeps it in her head and a whiteboard. I'd love a list every Monday of what's stuck and who we need to call.

AJ: What systems do you live in?

Carlos: AccuLynx for jobs, QuickBooks for the money. Homeowners mostly text us.

Carlos: Oh, and our crew guys ask for the material order the night before, and somebody types the order into the supplier website. Maybe two hours a week, not a big deal.

AJ: Anything you don't want the agent doing on its own?

Carlos: Nothing goes to an adjuster or a carrier without Tamara or me looking at it. Those relationships matter. And never tell a homeowner a dollar amount without me signing off.
